maria: Quick sync — proposing a split for 'hedge routing' responsibilities. Idea: policy returns an ordered candidate set with weights and an optional hints map. Runtime can optionally annotate with live capacity info. Need to decide interface boundary and migration approach. Thoughts?
kevin: I like separating concerns but worried about stale hints. If policy emits hints we risk making decisions on outdated telemetry. Prefer runtime-side annotation.
sam: Two-phase (policy->candidates, runtime->annotate/rescore) sounds clean but adds complexity and maybe an extra code path. Latency budget is the main risk. Could we speculatively annotate using cached probe state to avoid extra roundtrip? :thinking: 
rachel: Telemetry implications: we need a candidate_set_id and policy_version on every request so we can attribute outcomes to policy vs runtime. Current dashboards don't let us compare candidate-level outcomes.
maria: Good point. POC: policy_eval returns candidate_set_id (uuid) + candidates[]. Runtime attaches candidate_set_id to traces and metrics. That way sim/harness can replay and correlate. I'll add candidate_set_id to the RFC draft.
kevin: For backward-compat, v1 policy continues returning candidates[]. v2 adds optional hints. Runtime must accept both. Recommend runtime treats hints as advisory and apply a feature-flagged re-score path.
maria: Agreed. So migration plan: runtime accepts hints no-ops for now, enable rescoring behind FF, run sim and canary, then flip default.
ton y: I can pick up the runtime change to accept hints and implement the rescoring toggle. Also propose tenant_tier gating: premium tenants can opt into rescoring; cheaper tiers keep minimal path for latency.
sam: I'll update the sim harness to emit candidate_set_id and simulate hint sources (policy/runtime/cache). We should add synthetic capacity-fluctuation scenarios.
rachel: Test plan: add regression tests that inject high variance latency and ensure fallback triggers before SLO breach. Also emit candidate-level success/fail counts to dashboards.
kevin: Small API decision: rename "penalty" to "weight" in the candidate proto to avoid double-negatives in code. Also add a lightweight hints schema: map<string,float> with documented keys ("estimated_free_gpus", "short_term_load").
maria: Example proto sketch in-thread: 
```
message Candidate {
  string model = 1;
  float weight = 2;
  map<string,float> hints = 3;
}
```
kevin: Also add telemetry tag "hint_source" with values [policy, runtime, cache] so we can filter.
deploy-bot: New patchset opened by tony:704 for runtime-accept-hints #456 (CI queued)
maria: Nice. Action items (short): 1) RFC update: candidate_set_id + rename penalty->weight + hints schema; 2) runtime change: accept hints, feature-flagged rescoring, tenant_tier gate; 3) sim/harness: emit candidate_set_id, synthetic capacity scenarios, hint_source variants; 4) dashboards: candidate-level metrics and new tags.
kevin: One more ops concern: ensure candidate_set_id doesn't add cardinality explosion in metrics. Suggest TTL on candidate_set tag and rollup keys (policy_version + tenant_tier + route_group) for most views.
sam: I'll implement TTL rollups in sim output.
rachel: For rollout: canary to 5% Dedicated traffic, monitor 95th percentile latency and failed-fallback rate. If regressions spike, auto-roll back.
maria: I'll draft the RFC update and include the migration checklist + canary playbook by EOD. Tagging reviewers. Thanks everyone.
